Everything is green and scoped. Implementation is complete and locally verified. Per the loop protocol, I've made no commits, PRs, or ledger entries — the goal loop owns delivery.

## Result
- **Goal/task:** G-20260728T103742822780Z-2514c606 / T-20260728T103742824401Z-f198cd24 — inject id-scoped mirror locks at task registration
- **Role:** Implementer
- **Status:** complete (implementation + local verification; loop owns commit/PR/merge)

## What changed
- **`scripts/shiki_tasks.py`** — Added `mirror_locks_for_task(task_id, goal_id, ledger_ids)`: a deterministic, id-scoped mirror lock set (task file, worktree, lock record, goal file, DAG, owned ledgers) — every entry a concrete single-file path, never a shared-namespace glob. Plus `injected_mirror_locks`, idempotent `inject_mirror_locks`, and `_refresh_lock_record_locks`. Wired injection into all registration/dispatch paths (`register_task_from_plan`, `cmd_issue_plan`, `try_acquire_locks`, `allocate_worktree_record`, `cmd_lock_acquire`, `cmd_worktree_allocate`).
- **`scripts/shiki_locks.py`** — Added `is_goal_scoped_mirror_lock` and a **same-goal exemption** in `active_lock_conflicts`: two sibling tasks may hold the identical goal-file/DAG mirror lock (shared read-only goal state) without a false conflict. Product/glob overlaps still conflict.
- **`scripts/mergegate_check.py`** — `_frozen_task_match_errors` now binds locks via `_frozen_locks_match_errors`: recomputes the injected set from the task's own ids and rejects any lock outside `frozen ∪ injected` (blocks `path:.shiki/**` and foreign task mirror locks) and any dropped frozen lock.
- **`tests/test_mirror_lock_injection.py`** (new, 20 tests) + assertions in `test_shiki_control_plane.sh`.

**Design note:** the scope requires the goal file + DAG in the mirror set, but same-goal tasks share those, so full set-disjointness is impossible. I resolved this as the acceptance intends — task-owned locks are strictly disjoint, and the shared goal-scoped locks are exempted from conflict detection so sibling tasks never falsely block each other (verified via `orchestrate_plan` dispatching both).

## Checklist status
- **TDD:** red → green; 20 new tests, all 7 acceptance checks covered
- **Code-review gate:** performed manually (the `/code-review` skill is user-triggered/model-invocation-disabled); fixed one self-caught regression (lock-record/task-locks desync breaking `dispatch_check`) and an import-ordering nit before finalizing
- **Full suite:** 432/432 Python tests pass; 32/34 shell tests pass

## Evidence
- Python: `Ran 432 tests ... OK`; new suite `Ran 20 tests ... OK`
- Shell: `test_shiki_control_plane`, `run_orchestrator`, `goal_loop`, `loop_e2e`, `loop_lock_guard`, contract/reconcile/mergegate tests all pass
- The 2 shell failures (`guardian_policy`, `runtime_auth`) reproduce identically on the clean base → pre-existing/environmental, not from this change
- All changes within declared locks; no writes to the real `.shiki` mirror

## Next action
- Loop runs the TDD gate (`test_command`) and code-review verifier, then owns commit/push/PR/merge.
- **Follow-up (out of my lock scope):** `validate_shiki.py`'s advisory `loop_lock_warnings` still recommends `path:.shiki/**` coverage, which is now semantically stale for id-scoped tasks. It's advisory-only (never blocks), but a future task locking `scripts/validate_shiki.py` should teach it to recognize id-scoped mirror coverage.
